reply.note: Reviewer: claude-opus-high (codex unavailable). Setup block passed (validate, compile --check, hash-inputs); cleanup verify ok, no mismatches. Inputs reviewed: /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/design/rev-1/out/prd.view.md against /srv/gp-v2/state/session-login/a3/design/source-request.txt, with /srv/gp-v2/a3 src/server.js, src/users.js and test/* read for context. Every request item SRC-001..SRC-009 maps to a requirement with acceptance scenarios. I traced the rate-limit scenarios by hand: LOGIN-003-AC1/AC2/AC5/AC6/AC8/AC9/AC10 are consistent with the DEC-003 arithmetic (Retry-After 60 and 30, eviction and pruning sizes, exactly 5 verifications under 8 concurrent requests under any settle interleaving). I found no BLOCKING or MAJOR defects. The findings are coverage gaps in acceptance scenarios, one user-visible deviation that the PRD accepts as RISK-006, and two places the spec leaves unstated. No files were edited.

findings.title: In-flight counting returns 429 before 5 failures have happened, against the literal SRC-004 rule, and the 'only way' rationale does not hold
findings.location: architecture > security > accepted_risks > RISK-006; DEC-003; LOGIN-003-AC9
findings.detail: The request says 'after 5 failed attempts for one username within 60 seconds further attempts return 429'. DEC-003 locks when 'timestamps + pending >= 5', so a correct-password attempt gets 429 with fewer than 5 failures, e.g. 1 counted failure plus 4 in flight. RISK-006 admits this: 'a correct-password attempt can get 429 with Retry-After 1 while counted failures plus in-flight attempts for its username reach 5, even if some of those in-flight attempts would succeed ... it is the price of keeping concurrent guesses within the requested 5 failures'. The user sees this, and the coverage table still marks SRC-004 plainly 'covered'. The rationale that it is the unavoidable price is not true: an attempt that is locked only by in-flight attempts could wait for them to settle and then be re-tested, which would keep the 5-failure bound without answering 429 early. Either change the design or record the deviation against SRC-004 with a rationale that holds.

findings.title: LOGIN-004 names the 413 path, but no acceptance scenario exercises it, and the 500 path is left out
findings.detail: The statement says: 'no issued token is ever written to stdout, stderr or any console method, on success, 401, 429, 503, 400 or 413 paths.' LOGIN-004-AC1 'when' covers a successful login, wrong-password, unknown-user, reaching 429, 'a malformed (invalid JSON) request containing a password string', and a 503 server. It sends no oversized (413) body containing a password, so the 413 path is untested. The rejected-verification path (500, DEC-005/DEC-008: 'verification rejections to 500, without logging or rethrowing') is missing from both the statement's path list and the scenario.

findings.title: LOGIN-005 has no tests for its upper limits and leaves several of its stated clauses unchecked
findings.detail: The statement rejects usernames 'longer than 64' and passwords 'longer than 1024' characters and bodies 'over 4096 bytes'. AC1 tests only the rejected side (65 / 1025), and AC2 tests a '5000-byte body'. No scenario shows that a 64-character username, a 1024-character password or a 4096-byte body is accepted, so an off-by-one that rejects valid input would pass. AC1 also never sends a null body, an empty password, a non-string password or a missing username, all of which DEC-009 lists. The clause 'rejected requests never count as failed attempts and never take a verification slot' is tested only for 400 counting (AC3). Nothing checks that 413 does not count, and nothing checks that 400/413 do not take a gate slot (for example via gate.active()/queued() or a full gate).

findings.title: The default for options.sessions is never stated, though two acceptance scenarios depend on it
findings.location: architecture > decisions > DEC-006; DEC-001; LOGIN-007-AC4; LOGIN-004-AC1
findings.detail: DEC-006 gives defaults only for 'options.now (... default Date.now)' and 'options.gate (... default createVerificationGate())'. DEC-001 says server.js 'passes options.users, options.sessions, options.now and options.gate' but gives no default for sessions. LOGIN-007-AC4 builds 'createServer({ users: createUserStore(USERS), gate })' with no sessions and expects 'alice returns 200 with a token'. The second server in LOGIN-004-AC1 also passes no sessions. Constraint 6 only requires createServer() to work. The PRD should state that the default is createSessionStore() per createServer instance.

findings.title: LOGIN-007-AC4 relies on verifyAsync calling the module-local hashPasswordAsync, which DEC-011 does not specify
findings.detail: AC4 replaces 'the hashPasswordAsync export of src/users.js with a wrapper that counts calls and returns a promise the test settles'. The test settles only 'the 4 dummy hashes', yet expects 'alice returns 200 with a token'. DEC-011 says only that verifyAsync 'resolves crypto.timingSafeEqual(await hashPasswordAsync(password, user.salt), user.hash)'. If an implementation calls the export through module.exports, as DEC-004 tells src/login.js to do, alice's verification hits the wrapper and never settles, so AC4 hangs until the 20 s test timeout. LOGIN-003-AC7 already allows for this with 'rose by at least 5'. DEC-011 should state that verifyAsync uses the module-local function, not the replaceable export.

findings.title: No acceptance scenario checks that a rejected (500) verification is not counted as a failure
findings.detail: LOGIN-007 says 'a rejected verification answers 500 {"error": "internal error"} and does not count'. DEC-003 repeats that 'verifications that reject (500), never count'. AC5 sends one rejected attempt each for u01 to u04 and checks only the 500 body and that the slots are freed. No scenario sends 5 or more rejected verifications for one username and then shows that a further attempt is not 429, so an implementation calling end(username, true) on rejection would pass.

findings.title: No acceptance scenario pins which status wins when a locked username arrives at a full gate
findings.detail: DEC-010 says 'The handler asks for a slot after validation and after the arrival check()', so a locked username gets 429 rather than 503 when the gate is full. LOGIN-007 says 'A request that finds 4 running and 16 waiting gets ... 503' without excluding locked usernames from that sentence, apart from the earlier 'non-locked requests wait'. The client sees a different status depending on this order, and no scenario fixes it (LOGIN-007-AC3 uses an unlocked alice).

findings.title: LOGIN-006 bundles three separate needs
findings.detail: 'The login behaviour is pinned by the six focused test files ..., and the existing GET /health, 404 and user-store tests keep passing; a non-POST request to /login returns the existing 404 {"error": "not found"}.' This combines test-file presence, regression of existing tests, and the DEC-007 routing behaviour in one requirement, so it is not singular.

findings.title: LOGIN-004-AC2 duplicates a check LOGIN-004-AC1 already makes
findings.detail: AC1 already performs 'a successful login for alice' and asserts 'no recorded output contains any submitted password string or the issued token'. AC2 ('alice logs in successfully' / 'no recorded output contains the token from the 200 body') adds nothing.

findings.title: Retry-After wording for a partly in-flight lock is ambiguous, and the 'pending at most 4' claim depends on an ordering the PRD does not fix
findings.detail: DEC-003 sets Retry-After as computed 'when 5 timestamps remain' and as 1 s 'when the lock is due only to attempts in flight'. A lock with 1 to 4 timestamps plus pending attempts fits neither phrase literally. RISK-006 implies 1 s applies, but DEC-003 should say so. resource_consumption also states 'a pending count of at most 4'. That holds only if the handler's end() runs before the gate's finally starts the next queued task, and DEC-003/DEC-010 do not fix that order ('calls end() once the verification settles' vs 'decrements active in a finally step and starts the oldest queued task'). Pending can briefly reach 5. The bounds still hold.

findings.title: 'characters' for the length limits is undefined for non-ASCII input
findings.detail: 'length 1..64 characters' / '1..1024 characters'. The text does not say whether this is JS string length (UTF-16 code units) or Unicode code points, so an implementation and a test could disagree on astral-plane input.
